# WASP-121 b: composite at the planet's orbit, Lyman continuum of Huang et al. 2023
# columns: wavelength [A]  flux at the planet [erg cm^-2 s^-1 A^-1]
# reference: Huang et al. (2023), ApJ 951, 123 (2023ApJ...951..123H), section 2.2.
# normalization: F(1-912 A) = 1.9906e+05 erg cm^-2 s^-1 at the planet = 0.74 x the Lyman
#           continuum flux 2.69e5 the paper states for its spectrum (the factor is
#           the Table 3 XUV multiplier on all flux below 1700 A, Lya line included).
#           The F_XUV = 1.6e6 of the same section is NOT used: the paper's band
#           fluxes (70-80, 80-91.2, 91.2-117 nm), its Figure 1 and its Table 3
#           energy-limited M_XUV = 0.16 M_p/Gyr all correspond to 2.69e5 (see the
#           builder docstring).
# part 1:   lambda < 1700 A: WHI 2008 solar reference spectrum (Woods et al. 2009,
#           GRL 36, L01101), column 'March 30 - April 4', irradiance at 1 au,
#           x 6.702463e+04; Lya window 1206-1226 A above its local continuum x 1.761493e-01 so
#           that the line flux is 7.400e+04 erg cm^-2 s^-1 (Huang section 2.2).
# part 2:   lambda >= 1700 A: MUSCLES v24 const-res SED of WASP-17 (F6V) x 1.205643e+19 so
#           that the bolometric flux at the planet is sigma T_eff^4 (R_star/a)^2 =
#           6.997273e+09 erg cm^-2 s^-1, T_eff = 6459 K, R_star = 1.4572 R_sun, a = 0.02545 au;
#           BOLOFLUX = 5.803769e-10 from the FITS header; 0 rows below zero set to 0.
#           Stands in for the LLmodels photosphere of the paper (not available).
# join:     neither part renormalized at 1700 A; measured f(1700.0)/f(1699.5) = 1.0637,
#           F(1700-1750 A)/F(1650-1700 A) = 3.4080.
# check:    band flux / (multiplier x paper value): 70-80 nm 0.821, 80-91.2 nm 0.813,
#           91.2-117 nm 0.801 (paper: 1.4e4, 3.6e4, 6.3e4).
# bins:     1 A bin averages throughout. coverage 0.5000 to 5000.0000 A, 5001 rows.
# built by inputdata/sed/build/build_wasp121b_composite_lyc_huang.py
